note: Headless, run by Claude on the bench harness (M3 Pro, DPR=2, vite 5173 + serve:static 3001, pak build/original/opensa rebuilt 2026-08-09 13:53 — 91 092 clutter objects). ONE scene, country-dusk, five single-scene sweeps. WHY: `dump-cell` showed the pak bakes the procobj layer into its cells while `updateClutter` also feeds `adapter.cellClutter` into an instanced render every frame, which would mean the clutter is drawn TWICE. NOT COMPARABLE as a cost record: three of the five arms ran while a full `sa` build saturated the CPU, so only the CONTENT columns (avgTriangles, avgDrawCalls) are read here — the 2026-08-09 A/A floor established content holds to 0.094 % while cost does not. RESULT — no double clutter: turning the runtime scatter off (`?procobj=0`) and sweeping the per-cell cap 1 -> 3000 both leave triangles unchanged to within 0.007 %, which is an order of magnitude BELOW this pair's own A/A drift (arm a vs a2, same config, 0.41 %). CAUSE, found afterwards and by construction: `convertProcObj` STRIPS every species it baked, so the built `data/procobj.dat` carries 9 rules of the source's 96, all `P_UNDERWATERBARREN`. The runtime layer is alive but has nothing to scatter on dry land, so this scene could not have printed non-zero — the positive control failed on the SITE, not on the instrument. Consequence for lod-procobj 013: clutter load on `opensa` is a BUILD-time quantity, and neither `?procobj` nor `?procobjLimit` is a lever for its streaming budget.
findings: No double clutter. The build strips what it bakes, so the two layers are disjoint by construction.

The `hitch` block shipped with this run and its tail columns DO carry signal where the averages do not: `maxMs` ranges 9.4-21 ms across five arms whose `avgMs` is 8.329-8.334 and whose `p95Ms` is 9-9.1. `blobMaxMs`/`uploadMaxMs`/`pendingMax` printed 0 on every arm — a settled leg streams nothing, so those three still need a positive control before a zero from them is read as evidence.
A/A drift on this pair, same config, same session: triangles 0.41 % (arm a vs a2). Larger than every effect measured here.
